title: Manus vs OpenManus: Which Should You Use?
summary: A practical comparison of Manus and OpenManus for builders choosing AI agent, coding, workflow, or evaluation tools.
author: OpenAgent.bot Editors
seoDescription: Compare Manus vs OpenManus: use cases, tradeoffs, first tests, and adoption advice for AI builders.
body: If you are comparing **Manus vs OpenManus**, the short answer is: Choose Manus for a hosted agent experience; choose OpenManus when openness, inspection, and self-hosting experiments matter more.
This comparison focuses on adoption fit rather than hype. The better tool is the one that matches your workflow surface, review process, and risk tolerance.
## Fast answer
| Question | Better fit | Why |
| Need hosted general-purpose AI agent experience? | [Manus](https://manus.im) | It is designed around that surface |
| Need open-source attempt at a Manus-style agent workflow? | [OpenManus](https://github.com/mannaandpoem/OpenManus) | It optimizes for a different workflow shape |
| Need a first evaluation? | Start with the narrower workflow | Small tests reveal failure modes faster than broad demos |
## Core difference

[Manus](https://manus.im) is best understood as hosted general-purpose AI agent experience. [OpenManus](https://github.com/mannaandpoem/OpenManus) is best understood as open-source attempt at a Manus-style agent workflow. That difference matters because both tools may be called AI agents, but they usually operate at different layers of the stack.

A good Manus vs OpenManus decision should begin with the work surface. Are you trying to edit code, operate a browser, orchestrate multiple agents, run local models, evaluate outputs, or preserve memory? Once that surface is clear, the choice becomes less abstract.
## When to choose Manus

Choose [Manus](https://manus.im) when your primary need aligns with hosted general-purpose AI agent experience. It is the better starting point if your first experiment can be expressed in its native workflow rather than forced into another tool's interface.
The main evaluation question is not whether Manus can do everything. It is whether it gives you enough control, logs, and repeatability for the task you actually want to run.
## When to choose OpenManus

Choose [OpenManus](https://github.com/mannaandpoem/OpenManus) when your primary need aligns with open-source attempt at a Manus-style agent workflow. It may be the better option if your team already works in the environment or architecture it assumes.
The tradeoff is that a better fit for one workflow can be a worse fit for another. Do not treat OpenManus as a drop-in replacement for Manus unless the action surface is genuinely similar.
## Comparison table
| Criteria | Manus | OpenManus |
| Primary fit | hosted general-purpose AI agent experience | open-source attempt at a Manus-style agent workflow |
| Best first test | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria |
| Review model | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access |
| Main risk | Assuming a demo generalizes to production | Assuming a demo generalizes to production |
| Adoption advice | Start with a sandbox | Start with a sandbox |
## Practical recommendation
Choose Manus for a hosted agent experience; choose OpenManus when openness, inspection, and self-hosting experiments matter more.

If your team is still unsure, run both tools against the same small task. Keep the task boring: one repository issue, one browser flow, one document set, one local model endpoint, or one evaluation suite. The winner is the tool that produces the most reviewable result with the least operational surprise.

## FAQ
### Is Manus better than OpenManus?
Not universally. Choose Manus for a hosted agent experience; choose OpenManus when openness, inspection, and self-hosting experiments matter more.
### Can Manus and OpenManus be used together?
Sometimes, but prove the simple version first. Combining tools too early can make failures harder to diagnose.
### What should I measure in a comparison?
Measure task completion, reviewability, setup time, permission control, repeatability, and recovery from failure. Those signals matter more than a polished demo.
### Which one is better for production?
The production answer depends on governance. Prefer the option that supports sandboxing, narrow permissions, audit trails, and a human review loop for your specific workflow.
